title: Fixing iptsd and Two-Finger Scroll (Surface Snapdragon X, ARM64)
body:
Initial problem
sudo systemctl restart iptsd failed with Unit iptsd.service not found
Two-finger scroll on the touchpad wasn't working
Cause

The installed .deb package (iptsd 3.1.0-1 arm64) didn't include the files needed for systemd and udev integration. The iptsd project doesn't use a single iptsd.service, but a template unit (iptsd@.service) automatically triggered by a udev rule when a valid hidraw device is detected.

The source repository cloned into ~/iptsd/ contained the template files (.in), but they had never been installed into the correct system paths.

Solution

1. Created the systemd unit file at /usr/lib/systemd/system/iptsd@.service:
[Unit]
Description=Intel Precise Touch & Stylus Daemon
Documentation=https://github.com/linux-surface/iptsd
StopWhenUnneeded=yes
BindsTo=%i.device

[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=/usr/bin/iptsd /%I

2. Created the udev rule at /etc/udev/rules.d/50-iptsd.rules:
SUBSYSTEM=="hidraw", ACTION=="add", TAG+="systemd", \
	PROGRAM="/usr/bin/iptsd-check-device --quiet $env{DEVNAME}", \
	PROGRAM="/bin/systemd-escape --path $env{DEVNAME}", \
	ENV{SYSTEMD_WANTS}+="iptsd@$result.service"

3. Reloaded systemd and udev, and re-triggered already-connected hidraw devices:
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo udevadm control --reload
sudo udevadm trigger --subsystem-match=hidraw --action=add

4. Verified the service had started automatically:
systemctl list-units | grep iptsd

Result: iptsd@dev-hidraw3.service showed as loaded active running.

5. Applied the recommended calibration generated by iptsd-calibrate:
sudo cp iptsd_calib_045E_0C77_1785392979_2mm.conf /etc/iptsd.d/91-calibration-045E-0C77.conf

Result

The iptsd service now starts automatically at boot via udev, and two-finger scroll on the touchpad works correctly.

Notes for the future
If the iptsd package is updated in the future from a new .deb built the same way, check that iptsd@.service and 50-iptsd.rules are still present (a "bare" update might not reinstall them).
To recalibrate in the future: sudo iptsd-calibrate /dev/hidrawX (find the right device with iptsd-find-hidraw).
